prompt: How many original colonies (and stripes on the flag)?
body: Thirteen colonies, thirteen stripes — and on the Great Seal: 13 stars, 13 arrows, 13 olive leaves, 13 olives, 13 steps on the pyramid, and 13 letters in both E PLURIBUS UNUM and ANNUIT COEPTIS. The founders committed to the bit.

prompt: How many states (and stars on the flag)?
body: Fifty states, fifty stars. The current 50-star flag debuted July 4, 1960, after Hawaii joined — designed by a 17-year-old for a school project. He got a B-.

prompt: How many amendments does the Constitution have?
body: Twenty-seven amendments. The 27th took 202 years to ratify — proposed in 1789, adopted in 1992, after a college student got a C on a paper arguing it was still live. He was right.

prompt: How many branches of government?
body: Three branches: legislative, executive, judicial. Madison's math: ambition counteracting ambition needs at least three players.

prompt: How many U.S. Senators does each state have?
body: Two per state, Wyoming and California alike — the Great Compromise of 1787, still compromising.

prompt: How many U.S. Senators are there in total?
body: One hundred Senators. Also one hundred civics questions on the naturalization test — the two are unrelated, but the symmetry is free.

prompt: How many voting members are in the House of Representatives?
body: 435 voting members — frozen by law since 1929. The country tripled; the House didn't.

prompt: How many electors are in the Electoral College?
body: 538 electors: 435 + 100 + 3 for D.C. (23rd Amendment). Yes, a famous statistics website is named after it.

prompt: How many electoral votes does it take to win the presidency?
body: 270 to win — half of 538, plus one. The most consequential majority in American arithmetic.

prompt: How many justices sit on the Supreme Court?
body: Nine justices — set by statute, not the Constitution. It has been 5, 6, 7, 9, and 10 over the years. Nine stuck.

prompt: How many years is a presidential term?
body: Four years per term. Also the 4th of July — the number does double duty every leap-year November.

prompt: How many years is a U.S. Senator's term?
body: Six years per Senate term. Also 6 of 10: the passing score on the naturalization civics test. This fair grades the same way.

prompt: How old do citizens have to be to vote?
body: Eighteen to vote — the 26th Amendment (1971), passed when the draft age and voting age finally had to agree.

prompt: How many articles does the Constitution have?
body: Seven articles. The whole operating system of a country in about 4,500 words — shorter than most terms-of-service agreements.

prompt: How many amendments are in the Bill of Rights?
body: Ten amendments in the Bill of Rights. Twelve were proposed; one became the 27th two centuries later, and one is still technically pending. Sleep well.

prompt: How many delegates signed the Declaration of Independence?
body: Fifty-six signers, pledging lives, fortunes, and sacred honor. Hancock signed big enough for all of them.

prompt: How many delegates signed the Constitution?
body: Thirty-nine signatures of 55 delegates — three refused over the missing bill of rights, and got one delivered in 1791.

prompt: In what year was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
body: 1776. The only year with its own musical, its own font of fireworks, and — as of 2026 — its own 250th birthday party.

prompt: In what year was the Constitution written?
body: 1787 — one Philadelphia summer, windows nailed shut for secrecy, no air conditioning. The document holds up better than the room did.

prompt: In 2026, how many years old is the United States?
body: 250 years — the semiquincentennial, which is also the hardest word at the party. This entire fair is the birthday card.

prompt: Which amendment repealed another amendment?
body: The 21st repealed the 18th (Prohibition) — the only amendment whose entire job is deleting a previous amendment. America's ctrl+Z.

title: 10 years, 2 terms
prompt: What is the maximum number of years one person can serve as President?
body: Ten years: the 22nd Amendment allows two elected terms (8) plus up to half of someone else's term (2) if you succeeded mid-term. American numerology's deepest cut.
